upstream.proposal:
Fix option source masking when source is unknown (aka undefined)

## Problem

A global option value with an unknown source fails to mask the leaf option value source in `.getOptionValueSourceWithGlobals()`

Fixes: #2651

## Solution

Unlikely to happen in practice, but is not as intended and a simple code change.

Test for presence of option value source, rather than value of option value source.

## ChangeLog

- fix: global option values with unknown source should mask local option value source in  `.getOptionValueSourceWithGlobals()`

evidence.contract: packet/C.patch correctly handles setter-created undefined sources: starting lib/command.js:setOptionValue delegates to setOptionValueWithSource, which creates an own source-map entry even for undefined. Frozen build/native/contract/preserve checks all exit 0. However opts() in property-storage mode emits every declared option key even when unset, whereas C checks only _optionValueSources. Static public counterexample: create a parent with storeOptionsAsProperties().option("--common <value>"), create sub, and set sub common to "child" with source "cli". sub.optsWithGlobals().common is undefined from the parent, but C returns "cli" because the parent has no source-map entry. This boundary is not covered by the frozen check details.
evidence.tests: packet/C.patch adds a meaningful CLI regression with a parent setOptionValueWithSource call omitting source; it would fail under the starting predicate. The renamed default-source test retains every assertion, and no protection is removed. The addition does not assert optsWithGlobals consistency or cover falsy/undefined values, property storage, or unknown sources at nested levels. In particular it misses the declared-but-unset property-storage mismatch described under contract. Frozen native exit is 0.
evidence.design: packet/C.patch is a minimal, localized predicate change with no unrelated production edits. Checking own source-map membership is consistent with setter-created unknown sources, but uses metadata presence as a proxy for the option keys actually merged by optsWithGlobals; these representations differ in property storage. The approach needs an additional adjustment for that boundary.
evidence.proposal: packet/C.md accurately identifies the main masking defect and describes its source-map membership approach. It contains a title and substantive body, with no unsupported successful-check claim. It omits verification information and material limitations, and does not explain how consistency with optsWithGlobals or alternate storage is ensured.

evidence.contract: packet/B.patch detects explicitly stored undefined sources, and setOptionValue delegates to setOptionValueWithSource, which writes a source entry (lib/command.js:931-950). Frozen build/native/contract/preserve exits are all 0. A material property-storage edge remains: p = new Command().storeOptionsAsProperties().option("--common <value>"); s = p.command("sub").option("--common <value>"); s.setOptionValueWithSource("common", "leaf", "cli"). p.opts() contains common: undefined despite having no source entry, so s.optsWithGlobals().common is undefined while B returns cli. This follows mechanically from opts() at lib/command.js:1914 and is corroborated by starting tests/options.opts.test.js expectations for unset property-stored options.
evidence.tests: The added tests/options.optsWithGlobals.test.js case parses a child CLI value against an explicitly set parent value with omitted source; it distinguishes the original bug. The renamed default-source test retains all assertions, and existing child-only checks remain intact. No added assertion compares optsWithGlobals, and no regressions cover nesting, falsy/undefined values or property storage, including the concrete remaining masking mismatch. Frozen native exit 0 confirms only the selected suite.
evidence.design: The single-line own-property check on _optionValueSources is small and matches the setter implementation without unrelated edits. It equates source-entry presence with value presence, which fails for property-storage values exposed by opts() without a setter-created source entry. No tests or protections are deleted.
evidence.proposal: packet/B.md clearly identifies the defect and explains checking source-entry presence, but provides no verification results or discussion of coverage and limitations. The frozen passing checks establish executable outcomes separately; they do not supply the missing PR communication.

evidence.contract: packet/A.patch fixes setter-created unknown sources: lib/command.js setOptionValue delegates to setOptionValueWithSource, which always creates a source-map key, including for undefined. Frozen build, native, contract and preserve exits are all 0. However, source-map presence is not value presence. Static counterexample: const p = new Command().storeOptionsAsProperties().option("--common <value>"); const s = p.command("sub").option("--common <value>"); p.common = "parent"; s.setOptionValueWithSource("common", "child", "cli"); s.optsWithGlobals().common is "parent", but A still returns "cli" for s.getOptionValueSourceWithGlobals("common"). opts() reads the parent property, while no parent source-map key exists. This counterexample was not executed.

Frozen focused native exit is 0. Coverage does not exercise value/source-map disagreement, property storage, or nested source masking; the new test asserts only source, not agreement with optsWithGlobals.
evidence.design: packet/A.patch makes a small, idiomatic own-property check and preserves traversal and source retrieval. It changes only lib/command.js and the focused test file, with no deleted assertions or weakened validation. Checking _optionValueSources rather than the values consumed by optsWithGlobals leaves the demonstrated property-assignment path unresolved.

It supplies no verification results or limitations, leaving review confidence unclear; proposal_observation is present, so this is an observed omission rather than unavailable text.
